mainTopic: Tearing on שבת in anger or over the dead (מקלקל vs. מתקן), and the importance of mourning a חכם or אדם כשר
overview: This עמוד opens with the last line of the previous סוגיא, then quotes a new משנה. The משנה says that tearing in anger or over one's dead is פטור, because every מקלקל is פטור, but damaging in order to fix is judged like fixing. It also gives the minimum שיעורים for several textile labors. The גמרא sets a ברייתא that calls such tearing חייב against the משנה. For tearing over the dead, it narrows the משנה's case step by step. The case becomes a relative one need not mourn, who is not a חכם or an אדם כשר, and whose death one did not witness. For tearing in anger, the משנה follows רבי שמעון and the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה on מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. רבי אבין explains that calming one's anger makes the act constructive. The case is then limited to a controlled show of anger meant to discipline one's household, since real rage is compared to עבודה זרה. The עמוד ends with teachings on the reward for crying over an אדם כשר and the punishment for neglecting a חכם's הספד. A new statement of רבי יוחנן about a brother who died begins and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Finishing the previous discussion: a pouch-like bulge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the previous סוגיא. Tearing in order to sew happens when the fabric bunches up like a pouch.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the fabric became like a pouch.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the previous discussion. It finishes an answer about when someone would tear cloth in order to sew it properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous עמוד, the גמרא asked when tearing in order to sew two stitches ever happens. The answer is a case where a seam forms a pouch-like bulge. You tear it so the fabric lies flat, and then you sew it. The tearing serves a building purpose, so it counts as real מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: where it made it / where it became

phrases.english: Where it became like a pouch.
phrases.notes: End of the previous סוגיא about tearing in order to sew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun on the previous עמוד.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tearing to fix a bunched-up seam is a constructive tear.

steps.title: The משנה: destructive acts are exempt, but damaging in order to fix is not
steps.stepSummary: Tearing in anger or over one's dead is פטור, like all מקלקלין. A מקלקל על מנת לתקן has the same שיעור as a מתקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who tears his clothes in anger, or over his dead, and anyone who acts destructively, is exempt. One who damages in order to fix has the same minimum amount as one who fixes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that destructive acts on שבת are פטור, unless the damage is done in order to build or fix something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids constructive מלאכה on שבת. Pure destruction is not the kind of work the Torah forbids, so a מקלקל is פטור. If the damage is a step toward fixing something, it counts as constructive, and the normal שיעור applies.

keyTerms.meaning: one who damages or acts destructively
in order to fix or improve
the minimum amount needed to be liable

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מקלקל פטור is a basic principle across all the מלאכות of שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who tears in his anger
or over his dead,
and all who act destructively are exempt.
And one who damages in order to fix,
his minimum amount is like one who fixes.
phrases.notes: He is liable, with the normal שיעור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Destructive acts are פטור. Damaging in order to fix is judged like fixing.

steps.title: The משנה: minimum amounts for whitening, combing, dyeing, spinning and weaving
steps.stepSummary: Whitening, combing, dyeing and spinning require a double סיט. Weaving two threads requires one סיט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The minimum for one who whitens, combs, dyes or spins is the full width of a double סיט. One who weaves two threads, his minimum is one סיט.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the minimum amounts for several wool and textile labors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סיט is the gap between the forefinger and middle finger when they are spread apart. The four preparation labors need twice that length. Weaving two threads needs only one סיט.

keyTerms.meaning: one who whitens or cleans wool
the span between the forefinger and middle finger

phrases.english: The minimum for one who whitens and one who combs
and one who dyes and one who spins
is the full width of a double סיט,
and one who weaves two threads,
his minimum is the full width of one סיט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with specific שיעורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A double סיט for the four preparation labors, and one סיט for weaving two threads.

steps.title: A ברייתא says tearing over the dead makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one who tears over his dead is חייב, yet still fulfills the מצוה of קריעה. This contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pointed out a contradiction: one who tears in his anger, in his mourning, or over his dead is liable. Even though he desecrates שבת, he has fulfilled the obligation of tearing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a ברייתא against the משנה. The משנה says פטור, and the ברייתא says חייב for the same act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats tearing over the dead as pure destruction, so it is פטור. The ברייתא calls it חייב and says the מצוה of קריעה is fulfilled. That suggests the tear is a meaningful, constructive act. Both sources cannot be right about the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: and they pointed out a contradiction
he fulfilled the obligation of tearing

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they pointed out a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: הַקּוֹרֵעַ בַּחֲמָתוֹ וּבְאֶבְלוֹ וְעַל מֵתוֹ — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: One who tears in his anger, in his mourning, or over his dead is liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּחַלֵּל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and even though he desecrates שבת,
he has fulfilled the obligation of tearing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that tearing over one's dead is פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules חייב for the identical act.

steps.title: Answer: one's own dead versus someone else's dead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא (חייב) speaks of one's own dead. The משנה (פטור) speaks of any other dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about his own dead, and that one is about a dead person in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא splits the two sources into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing for one's own relative fulfills a real obligation, so the tear accomplishes something. That makes it constructive, and it is חייב. Tearing for a stranger accomplishes nothing required, so it is just destruction, and it is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: a dead person in general, not his relative

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about his own dead,
that one is about a dead person in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּמֵת דִּידֵיהּ, הָא בְּמֵת דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the sources into different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources discuss the same kind of dead person.
steps.terutzMaskana: Obligatory tearing is חייב. Non-obligatory tearing is פטור.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא with "חייב" is the one about one's OWN dead, not the משנה. Tearing when you are obligated counts as a constructive act.

steps.title: But the משנה says "his dead"
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's wording, מתו, means his own dead, so it cannot refer to a stranger.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches "his dead"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 5 using the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says "מתו" (his dead), which clearly means his own relative. So the משנה cannot be about a stranger, and the previous answer seems to collapse.

phrases.english: But it teaches "his dead"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה refers to a stranger
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word "מתו" contradicts that reading.

steps.title: His own dead, but a relative he does not have to mourn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה speaks of one's own relative who is not among the relatives one must mourn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is about his own dead, but about those who are not subject to mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the word "his dead" but narrows the case to a relative one has no mourning obligation for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real test is not whether the dead person is related. The test is whether one is obligated to tear. A relative outside the mourning obligation creates no duty to tear, so tearing for him is still destructive, and it is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: those one is obligated to mourn

phrases.english: Really, it is about his own dead,
but about those who are not subject to mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by refining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "His dead" must mean a relative he has to mourn.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a relative he does not have to mourn, so the tear is not obligatory.

steps.title: But if the dead person is a חכם, everyone must tear
steps.stepSummary: If the dead person is a חכם, tearing is obligatory, because a ברייתא says that when a חכם dies, everyone is his relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is a חכם, one is obligated, as it was taught: when a חכם dies, everyone is his relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. Even a non-mourning relative must tear if the dead person was a חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a חכם dies, tearing is required of everyone. So in that case the tear is obligatory and should be חייב. The משנה's blanket פטור seems to ignore this.

phrases.english: And if he is a Torah scholar,
one is certainly liable,
as it was taught: a scholar who died,
everyone is his relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that tearing for a non-mourning relative is never obligatory
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the dead person is a חכם, tearing is obligatory for everyone.

steps.title: Can everyone really be his relative?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the literal wording of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is his relative? Could that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question the ברייתא's wording. This sets up a corrected reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Literally, not everyone is related to the חכם. So the wording must mean something else.

phrases.english: Everyone is his relative? Could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side point about the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not everyone is literally related to the חכם.

steps.title: Corrected reading: everyone is like his relatives
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא should read: everyone is like his relatives. All tear, all bare the shoulder, and all eat the mourner's meal in the square.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: everyone is like his relatives. Everyone tears over him, everyone bares his shoulder over him, and everyone eats the mourner's meal over him in the town square.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording and lists the mourning practices everyone does for a חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word becomes "כקרוביו", meaning everyone acts like a relative. This includes קריעה, חליצת כתף and הבראה. So the challenge from step 8 still stands: tearing for a חכם is obligatory.

keyTerms.meaning: they bare the shoulder in mourning
they eat the mourner's first meal (סעודת הבראה)

phrases.english: Rather, say: everyone is like his relatives,
everyone tears over him,
everyone bares the shoulder over him,
everyone eats the mourner's meal over him in the square.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 and restores the force of step 8.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone acts like a relative, including tearing.

steps.title: The משנה is about someone who is not a חכם
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's פטור applies only when the dead relative is not a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed where he is not a Torah scholar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 8. The משנה's case is a non-mourning relative who is not a חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only when no obligation to tear exists is the tear purely destructive. So the משנה's case has two conditions: a relative one need not mourn, and a person who is not a חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for (a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: Tearing on שבת over a dead person is חייב when the tear is obligatory: for a close relative or for a חכם. It is פטור as a מקלקל only when there is no obligation to tear.

phrases.english: It is only needed
where he is not a Torah scholar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's פטור includes a חכם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה applies only to a non-mourning relative who is not a חכם.

steps.title: Tearing over an upright person is an obligation
steps.stepSummary: If the dead relative was an אדם כשר, tearing is obligatory. So why does the משנה call it פטור?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he was an upright person, one is obligated to tear. As a ברייתא teaches: Why do a person's sons and daughters die when they are young? So that he will cry and mourn over an upright person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the משנה's case. If the dead person was an אדם כשר, everyone is required to tear, so the tearing should count as a real, useful act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 limited the משנה to a dead relative who is not a חכם. Now the גמרא points out that even an ordinary אדם כשר requires tearing, based on a ברייתא that stresses how important it is to mourn him. An obligatory tearing is a constructive act, which would make one חייב on שבת.

phrases.english: And if he is an upright person
one is obligated (to tear)
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
Why do the sons and daughters die
of a person when they are young?
So that he will cry and mourn
over an upright person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָדָם כָּשֵׁר הוּא חַיּוֹבֵי מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a further obligation-to-tear case after the חכם case was set aside
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that tearing over one's dead relative is פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tearing over an אדם כשר is obligatory and therefore constructive, so it should be חייב on שבת

steps.title: Do children die as a pledge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording of the ברייתא: do children die just so that the father will cry?
steps.simpleTranslation: So that he will cry?! Is a security deposit being taken from him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question how the ברייתא is worded. It cannot be that children die in advance just to make sure a person will cry later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the ברייתא literally, the children's death sounds like a pledge taken ahead of time to guarantee he will mourn. That makes no sense, so the wording must be fixed.

phrases.english: So that he will cry?!
Do they take a pledge from him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question on the wording of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase כדי שיבכה in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Punishment in advance to secure a future act is illogical

steps.title: Corrected reading: because he did not mourn
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is corrected: children die because the father failed to cry over an אדם כשר. Whoever does cry is forgiven for all his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: because he did not cry and mourn over an upright person. For anyone who cries over an upright person is forgiven for all his sins, because of the honor he showed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording. The children's death is a punishment for not mourning, not a pledge for the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The corrected version shows how serious mourning an אדם כשר is. It is so great that it brings forgiveness of all one's sins. This confirms the point of step 12: mourning and tearing for an אדם כשר is a real obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor he showed (to the dead)

phrases.english: Rather: because he did not cry
and mourn over an upright person,
for anyone who cries over an upright person
is forgiven for all his sins
because of the honor he showed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question by emending the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Children die as a guarantee that the father will mourn
steps.terutzMaskana: Children die as punishment for failing to mourn an אדם כשר

steps.title: The משנה speaks of someone not upright
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's פטור applies when the dead person was not an אדם כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where he was not an upright person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 12. The משנה is talking about a dead relative who was not an אדם כשר, so there is no obligation to tear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an obligation, the tearing is purely destructive, so the משנה can call it פטור. The משנה's case keeps getting narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only (for this specific case)

phrases.english: It is needed only
where he was not an upright person.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּלָאו אָדָם כָּשֵׁר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the wording side-question to answer step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could include an אדם כשר, which would make tearing obligatory
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks only of a dead person who was not an אדם כשר

steps.title: Present at the moment of death requires tearing
steps.stepSummary: Anyone standing by a person when the soul departs must tear, like over a burned ספר תורה. So why would the משנה's tearing be פטור?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he was standing there at the moment the soul left, he is obligated. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: one who stands by the dead at the moment the soul leaves must tear. To what is this compared? To a Torah scroll that was burned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another case where tearing is required: being present at the moment of death. If the משנה includes that case, the tearing would again be obligatory and constructive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר compares a Jewish soul leaving the body to a burned ספר תורה, which requires tearing. So even a non-upright relative creates an obligation to tear if one was present at death.

keyTerms.meaning: The departure of the soul (moment of death)
A Torah scroll that was burned

phrases.english: And if he stood there at the moment the soul left
he is obligated (to tear),

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: הָעוֹמֵד עַל הַמֵּת בִּשְׁעַת יְצִיאַת נְשָׁמָה —
phrases.english: one who stands by the dead at the moment the soul leaves
is obligated to tear;
to what is this similar?
To a Torah scroll that was burned!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי דְּקָאֵי בִּשְׁעַת יְצִיאַת נְשָׁמָה חַיּוֹבֵי מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After excluding an אדם כשר, raises another case where tearing is obligatory
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's פטור for tearing over one's dead relative
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Presence at death makes tearing obligatory and constructive, so it should be חייב

steps.title: The משנה speaks of someone not present at death
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's פטור applies when one was not present at the moment of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where he was not standing there at the moment the soul left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers again by narrowing the case. The משנה speaks of someone who was not there when the person died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה's case is very specific. It is a relative one need not mourn, who was not a חכם and not an אדם כשר, and whose death one did not witness. Only then is the tearing pointless and destructive, and therefore פטור.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case of tearing על מתו as פטור is limited to a dead person one need not tear for at all: not a required relative, not a חכם, not an אדם כשר, and not witnessed at death.

phrases.english: It is needed only
where he was not standing there at the moment the soul left.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּלָא קָאֵי בִּשְׁעַת יְצִיאַת נְשָׁמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could include one present at death, who is obligated to tear
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks only of one not present at death

steps.title: The anger contradiction still stands
steps.stepSummary: The dead-relative contradiction is solved, but the contradiction about tearing בחמתו remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for 'his dead.' But 'his anger' against 'his anger' is still difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the contradiction. The משנה says tearing in anger is פטור, while the ברייתא says it is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the narrowing so far dealt only with tearing over a dead relative. Tearing in anger has no obligation to narrow away, so the clash between the משנה and the ברייתא still needs an answer.

phrases.english: This works for 'his dead,'
but 'his anger' against 'his anger' is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח מֵתוֹ, אֶלָּא חֲמָתוֹ אַחֲמָתוֹ קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the resolved מתו contradiction to the unresolved חמתו contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: The conflict between the משנה (פטור) and the ברייתא (חייב) about tearing in anger
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings on the same act

steps.title: A dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה (מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is חייב). The משנה follows רבי שמעון (it is פטור).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His anger' against 'his anger' is also not difficult. This one follows רבי יהודה and that one follows רבי שמעון. This follows רבי יהודה, who says a labor not needed for its own purpose is liable. That follows רבי שמעון, who says a labor not needed for its own purpose is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the anger contradiction by assigning each source to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing in anger is not done for the normal purpose of tearing (preparing the cloth to be sewn), so it is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. רבי יהודה holds one is חייב for such a labor, which matches the ברייתא. רבי שמעון holds one is פטור, which matches the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A labor done not for its own normal purpose

steps.whyThisMatters: This links tearing in anger to the major שבת principle of מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, which matters across all of הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: 'His anger' against 'his anger' is also not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא — רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Yehuda, that is Rabbi Shimon.
This is Rabbi Yehuda, who said

phrases.aramaic: מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵין צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ — חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ.
phrases.english: a labor not needed for its own sake is liable.
That is Rabbi Shimon, who said

phrases.aramaic: מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵין צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ — פָּטוּר עָלֶיהָ.
phrases.english: a labor not needed for its own sake is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמָתוֹ אַחֲמָתוֹ נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא contradict each other on the same view
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון on מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה say this even for a destructive act?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's liability may apply only to a constructive act, but tearing in anger is destructive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say you heard רבי יהודה rule this way regarding a constructive act. Did you hear him say so regarding a destructive act?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 19. Maybe רבי יהודה holds one liable only when the act is constructive, and tearing in anger seems destructive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a purely destructive act (מקלקל) is generally פטור. So even רבי יהודה might exempt tearing in anger, and the ברייתא's חייב would be left without an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: One who does a constructive act
One who does a destructive act
Say that you heard him (say so)

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בִּמְתַקֵּן,
phrases.english: Say you heard Rabbi Yehuda say this about a constructive act;
about a destructive act, did you hear him say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בִּמְתַקֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the attribution of the ברייתא to רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's liability may be limited to constructive acts, and tearing in anger is destructive

steps.title: Tearing in anger calms him, so it is constructive
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין says tearing in anger is constructive because it soothes the person's temper.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: This too is constructive, because he gives satisfaction to his inclination (calms his anger).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין answers that tearing in anger is not purely destructive. It achieves something: it calms the angry person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the person gains real benefit (cooling his anger), the act counts as מתקן. So רבי יהודה can hold him חייב, and the attribution of step 19 stands.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said:
This too is constructive,
since he gives satisfaction to his inclination.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין: הַאי נָמֵי מְתַקַּן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the act (destructive act reclassified as constructive)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tearing in anger is purely destructive
steps.terutzMaskana: It is constructive because it calms the person's anger

steps.title: Is tearing in anger even permitted?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one who tears, breaks, or scatters things in anger is like an idol worshipper. So how can the גמרא treat calming one's anger this way as legitimate?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is such a thing permitted? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of חילפא בר אגרא, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן בן נורי: One who tears his clothes, breaks his vessels, or scatters his money in anger should be in your eyes like one who worships idols. For this is the craft of the יצר הרע: today it tells him do this, tomorrow it tells him do that, until it tells him to worship idols, and he goes and worships.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבין's picture of satisfying one's anger by tearing. A ברייתא strongly condemns acting out in anger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין treated calming one's anger as a real benefit that makes the act constructive. But the ברייתא says giving in to anger is the יצר הרע's step-by-step path toward עבודה זרה. That suggests such tearing is forbidden behavior, not a legitimate benefit. Step 24 answers this challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי אבין's answer was rejected. The גמרא answers this challenge in step 24, on this same עמוד: the case is someone who tears deliberately to instill fear in his household, not someone overcome by rage.

phrases.english: And is it permitted in such a manner?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says
in the name of Ḥilfa bar Agra,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:
phrases.english: who said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri:
One who tears his clothes in his anger,
or who breaks his vessels in his anger,
or who scatters his money in his anger,
should be in your eyes like an idol worshipper.
For such is the craft of the evil inclination:
today it tells him, 'Do this,'
and tomorrow it tells him, 'Do that,'

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁאוֹמֵר לוֹ עֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
phrases.english: until it tells him, 'Worship idols,'
and he goes and worships.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבין's premise that satisfying one's anger is a legitimate benefit
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבין's claim that tearing to calm one's anger counts as a constructive benefit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acting out in anger is condemned as a path to עבודה זרה, so it cannot be treated as a legitimate, beneficial act

steps.title: The verse behind the ברייתא: the strange god inside you
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין brings a פסוק showing that the 'strange god' within a person is the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: What is the verse? 'There shall be no strange god within you, and you shall not bow to a foreign god.' What strange god is inside a person's body? You must say: this is the יצר הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין gives a scriptural source for the ברייתא's idea. Giving in to the יצר הרע is linked to idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks of a strange god 'within you,' and the only 'god' inside a person is the יצר הרע. Obeying it is therefore close to worshipping a foreign god, which supports the ברייתא's harsh comparison.
steps.whatToRemember: Tearing in anger is בחמתו: the משנה (רבי שמעון) exempts it and the ברייתא (רבי יהודה) holds it liable, since רבי אבין says calming anger makes it constructive. Yet giving in to anger is sharply condemned as serving the 'strange god within,' the יצר הרע.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said: What is the verse?
'There shall not be a strange god within you,
and you shall not bow to a foreign god.'
What is the strange god
that is within a person's body?
You must say: this is the evil inclination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides scriptural grounding for the ברייתא quoted in the challenge
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's comparison of acting in anger to עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים פא:י, 'לא יהיה בך אל זר'

steps.title: Tearing done deliberately to make the household afraid
steps.stepSummary: The case of liability is someone who is not really losing control. He tears on purpose to make his household fear him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is needed only where he does it to put fear into the members of his household.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 22. Tearing in real rage is like עבודה זרה, but our case is a person who is calm inside and stages the tearing to discipline his household.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 22 condemned a person who is overcome by the יצר הרע. Here the person is fully in control and acts for a purpose. So the act is not the 'strange god' of real rage. Because it achieves something he wants, it still counts as a constructive act for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for… (introduces a narrower case that fits the ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say real anger is permitted. The person described here is NOT actually angry. He is only showing anger in a controlled way so his household listens.

phrases.english: It is only necessary
where he does it to cast fear
phrases.notes: He acts on purpose and is not overcome by emotion.

phrases.english: upon the members of his household.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Steps 22–23 by narrowing the case of tearing in anger to a staged, controlled display.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tearing in anger always means losing control to the יצר הרע, which is like עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our case is deliberate, controlled 'anger' meant to discipline the household. That is legitimate and purposeful.

steps.title: Stories of sages who staged small acts of anger
steps.stepSummary: Four אמוראים showed anger through acts that caused almost no real damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב יהודה, who pulled threads off his garment. רב אחא בר יעקב broke vessels that were already broken. רב ששת threw small fish at his maidservant's head. רבי אבא broke the lid of a jug.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with examples of great sages who acted angry on purpose. Each one chose an act that did almost no harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each act was picked to look angry while causing little or no loss: loose threads, broken vessels, small fish, a cheap lid. This shows the sages were fully in control, which matches the controlled case described in Step 24.

phrases.english: Like that of Rav Yehuda
who pulled off threads
phrases.notes: From his garment, causing minimal damage.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב תָּבַר מָאנֵי תְּבִירֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov broke already-broken vessels,
Rav Sheshet threw at his maidservant
small fish onto her head,
Rabbi Abba broke a jug lid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports the answer of Step 24 with real-life examples.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can show anger in a controlled, purposeful way.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Actions of רב יהודה, רב אחא בר יעקב, רב ששת, and רבי אבא.
steps.whatToRemember: Tearing 'in anger' counts as constructive for רבי יהודה when the anger is controlled and has a goal, such as calming oneself or disciplining one's household. Real, uncontrolled rage is compared to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: God counts and stores tears shed for a righteous person
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches that הקב"ה counts tears cried over an אדם כשר and keeps them in His treasury.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoting בר קפרא: Anyone who sheds tears over a proper person, הקב"ה counts those tears and places them in His treasure-house. As it says: 'You have counted my wanderings; put my tears into Your flask; are they not in Your book?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new related topic: mourning for a worthy person. It quotes a teaching about how precious such tears are to הקב"ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the earlier discussion of tearing קריעה over an אדם כשר or a חכם. The פסוק speaks of tears in God's 'flask' and 'book', which shows they are counted and saved.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, in the name of Bar Kappara:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַמּוֹרִיד דְּמָעוֹת עַל אָדָם כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: Anyone who sheds tears over an upright person,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, counts them
and places them in His treasury,
as it is stated: “You have counted my wanderings,
put my tears into Your flask,
are they not in Your book?” (Tehillim 56:9)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a related topic: mourning for worthy people, connected to the earlier laws of קריעה for the dead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tears shed over an אדם כשר are counted and treasured by הקב"ה.

steps.title: Being lazy in eulogizing a sage deserves death
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that someone lazy in the הספד of a חכם deserves to be buried alive. This is learned from the mountain that 'raged' at יהושע's burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who is lazy in eulogizing a חכם deserves to be buried alive. As it says: 'They buried him in the border of his inheritance in תמנת סרח, which is in הר אפרים, north of הר געש.' This teaches that the mountain raged against them to kill them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, sharper teaching about mourning: failing to properly eulogize a חכם is a grave sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name הר געש ('raging mountain') is read as a hint. The mountain 'raged' (רגש) against Israel because they did not properly mourn יהושע. If the mountain wanted to kill them, such people deserve death.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Anyone who is lazy in the eulogy of a Sage —
it is fitting to bury him alive,
as it is stated: “And they buried him in the border of his inheritance
in Timnat-serach, which is in the hill country of Ephraim,
north of Mount Ga'ash” (Yehoshua 24:30),
this teaches that the mountain raged against them to kill them.
phrases.notes: The word געש is being read as if it were related to רגש, 'to rage'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the mourning theme, moving from the reward for crying to the punishment for neglecting a חכם's הספד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neglecting the הספד of a חכם is so severe that the person deserves to be buried alive.

steps.title: Neglecting a sage's eulogy shortens one's life
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that one who is lazy in a חכם's הספד does not live long. This is מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who is lazy in eulogizing a חכם will not live long. It is measure for measure, as it says: 'In full measure, when You send her away, You contend with her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching on the same theme. This one gives a specific punishment: a shortened life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this person did not care about the death of the חכם, Heaven does not care to extend his life. The word בסאסאה (from סאה, a measure) teaches that הקב"ה punishes measure for measure. This מימרא sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: measure for measure (punishment matching the sin)
in full measure (from סְאָה, a unit of measure)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who is lazy in the eulogy of a Sage
does not live long —
measure for measure,
as it is stated: “In full measure, when You send her away, You contend with her” (Yeshayahu 27:8).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching on the same subject, with a different punishment: a shortened life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who neglects a חכם's הספד does not live long, as a measure-for-measure punishment.

steps.title: The elders who neglected יהושע still lived long
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא challenges רבי יוחנן: the זקנים did not properly mourn יהושע, yet the פסוק says they 'lengthened days'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא challenged רבי יוחנן: It says, 'The people served ה׳ all the days of יהושע, and all the days of the elders who lengthened days after יהושע.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן's own student challenges him from a פסוק. The זקנים neglected יהושע's הספד, as Step 27 showed, yet they seem to have lived long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to Step 27, the generation of יהושע was lazy in his הספד. If רבי יוחנן is right, the זקנים should have died early. But the פסוק says they הֶאֱרִיכוּ יָמִים, 'lived many days', which seems to contradict him.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיַּעַבְדוּ הָעָם אֶת ה׳ כֹּל יְמֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: “And the people served ה׳ all the days of Yehoshua
and all the days of the elders
who lengthened days after Yehoshua” (Shoftim 2:7)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the מימרא of Step 28 using a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that one who neglects a חכם's הספד does not live long.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The זקנים neglected יהושע's הספד, yet the פסוק says they 'lengthened days'. That contradicts the rule.

steps.title: They lengthened days, not years
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the פסוק says 'days', not 'years'. They lived a few extra days but not extra years.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Babylonian! They lengthened days; they did not lengthen years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by reading the exact word of the פסוק. It says 'days', which means only a short extension.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יָמִים is read narrowly. The זקנים outlived יהושע by days, but they did not survive many years. So the פסוק actually fits the punishment. Calling him בבלאי is a gentle push to read more carefully.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonian! (a mild rebuke to read more precisely)

phrases.english: He said to him: Babylonian!
They lengthened days; they did not lengthen years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 29 through a precise reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Lengthened days' means they lived long lives.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Days' means only a short extension, not long years. So they were still punished.

steps.title: Does the blessing of long life also mean only days?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא pushes back: if 'days' means only a little, then the Torah's blessing of 'multiplied days' would mean only days and not years.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, what about 'So that your days and the days of your children may multiply' — does that mean days and not years?
steps.whatsHappening: The challenger turns the new reading against itself. He points to a blessing in the Torah that also uses the word 'days'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יָמִים always means a short time, then the blessing of long life in קריאת שמע would be a tiny reward. That cannot be right. So the reading 'days, not years' seems too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, according to your reasoning… (shows an unacceptable result)

phrases.english: But now, according to this:
“So that your days and the days of your children may multiply” (Devarim 11:21) —
days and not years?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 30 by showing it leads to an absurd reading of another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that יָמִים means only days, not years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applied to the blessing of long life, this reading would shrink the blessing to almost nothing, which is impossible.

steps.title: A blessing is read generously
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that a blessing is different and is understood in its broadest sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blessing is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers briefly: when the Torah gives a blessing, 'days' is read in the most generous way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How a word is read depends on its context. In a blessing, 'days' means long years of life. In a description of people who deserved punishment, it is read narrowly. So both פסוקים stand, and רבי יוחנן's rule holds.
steps.whatToRemember: Neglecting the הספד of a חכם is a severe sin, and רבי יוחנן says it shortens one's life. The זקנים after יהושע only 'lengthened days', meaning they lived briefly. When the Torah promises a blessing of 'days', it means a long life, because a blessing is read generously.

phrases.english: A blessing is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 31 by distinguishing a blessing context from a punishment context.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word יָמִים must mean the same thing everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a blessing, 'days' is read broadly as long years. Elsewhere it can be read narrowly.

steps.title: A new teaching begins about a brother who died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן begins a new teaching about the case when one of several brothers dies. The rest continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: When one of the brothers dies —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next teaching of רבי יוחנן, also about mourning. The statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְאָמַר links this to the same pair of speakers, רבי חייא בר אבא quoting רבי יוחנן. Only the opening case is given here, a brother who died. The ruling about how the other brothers should react comes next.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one of the brothers dies —
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new מימרא from the same speakers, continuing the theme of mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening case only: a brother who died. The ruling follows in the next section.
